items.a: Finding true/false values that satisfy clauses of **three variables** like **(A or B or C)**.

items.q: What does the exponential time hypothesis claim?
items.a: That 3-SAT **can't be solved faster than exponential time**.

items.q: Does a sub-exponential algorithm make 3-SAT practical?
items.a: No: it's **still exponential-scale** and impractical, just **slower-growing**.
Its answer can be **verified in polynomial time**.
It's in NP and **at least as hard as every NP problem**, so all NP-complete problems **reduce to each other**.

items.q: Why would P = NP threaten encryption?
items.a: Problems like **factoring** behind **RSA** could be solved fast.
